items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: I mean this kid, and I had an opportunity to profile him.

ctx.x: Oh you’ve got to check him out. I mean this kid, and I had an opportunity to profile him. He literally — he’s a savant and he’s learned Bird solos, Coltrane solos, Dexter Gordon solos. Note for note. And he’s done it this way. He doesn’t follow the process of looking at a transcription, playing the notes and then you know, he goes the other way, which is of course the way a lot of older players have learned you know. But I’ll tell you, as an educator, one little trick that I’ve used with a lot of success — and…

and then that two notes becomes a little more involved rhythmically and you try to keep it within the technical abilities of the student, which is of course the teacher’s responsibility, and then you tell the student, “You know what you have done? You have just played jazz. You have just improvised, okay?” And then you — and again this is things that have worked. I mean there are things that I’ve done that just fell flat as a flat tire okay. But you want to get the child or the student feeling confident about…
